paper_a.title: On Serre's modularity conjecture for 2-dimensional mod $p$ representations of $\mathrm{Gal}(\bar{\mathbb{Q}}/\mathbb{Q})$ unramified outside $p$

paper_b.title: On Serre's reciprocity conjecture for 2-dimensional mod $p$ representations of $\mathrm{Gal}(\bar{\mathbb{Q}}/\mathbb{Q})$

metadata.description: Paper A (Khare, sole author) is the unconditional proof of the level-1 case of Serre's modularity conjecture. Paper B (Khare-Wintenberger) develops the foundational deformation-theoretic and compatible-system machinery and uses it to obtain (i) several unconditional partial results (low weights, low conductors, weight-12 from Ramanujan Delta) and (ii) two CONDITIONAL reduction theorems showing modularity-lifting hypotheses imply level-1 Serre and that level-1 Serre plus modularity lifting implies the squarefree-conductor case. Paper A extends paper B by removing the modularity-lifting assumption in the level-1 case via an inductive Chebyshev / foil-prime weight-reduction argument, citing paper B repeatedly as [KW] for the low-weight base cases and the lifting-and-compatible-system technology. The pair therefore exhibits a clean EXT relation: paper A turns paper B's conditional level-1 reduction (TP393.8) into the unconditional Theorem TP392.1.

matches.explanation: Both define a 'lift of the residual representation $\bar\rho$' as a continuous representation $\rho: G_\mathbb{Q}\to\mathrm{GL}_2(V)$ over the integers of a finite extension of $\mathrm{Frac}(W(\mathbb{F}))$, reducing to $\bar\rho$ mod the maximal ideal. Identical formulation.

Both papers use the same notion of minimally ramified lift in the sense of Diamond [D97] at primes $\ell\neq p$, and prescribe a specific local condition at $p$. Paper A's `Minimal at $\ell\neq p$' (DP392.2) and `Minimal of weight 2 at $p$' (DP392.5) together cover the same content as paper B's `Minimally ramified lift at $\ell$' (DP393.3) and `Minimally ramified deformation' (DP393.4). Both flag the special $k(\bar\rho)=p+1$ semistable-vs-crystalline dichotomy, paper B more explicitly.

Paper A's `Modular representation' definition (DP392.3) and paper B's `Serre type representation' (DP393.1) plus the formal statement of Serre's conjecture (ProbP393.1) describe the same object: an odd irreducible 2-dim mod-$p$ Galois representation, conjecturally arising from a newform of optimal level/weight. The two papers package it slightly differently (one as a definition of `modular', the other as `Serre type' + conjecture) but agree on content.

Both define `semistable mod-$p$ representation' as one with unipotent ramification at primes $\neq p$. Paper B additionally requires Serre weight $\le p+1$ at $p$ (a minor technical strengthening that comes for free after twisting in the Section 2 setup of paper B); same content.

Paper A's `Linked compatible systems' (DP392.4) is the relation that two compatible systems share semisimplified residual representation at a prime, used to transfer modularity. Paper B's `Strictly compatible system' (DP393.5) and `Minimal strictly compatible system lifting $\bar\rho$' (DP393.6) are the foundational definitions of the systems themselves. They are related notions (linking is a relation between such systems) rather than literally the same definition; both serve the same role in the workflow of `lift + compatible system + reduce + lift' that is shared between the papers.

Paper A's notion of `dihedral representation' (projective image dihedral) is an internal building block of Khare's Lemma LP392.1 (Wintenberger's lemma). Paper B does not extract it as a separate definition; the dihedral case is handled implicitly through Lemma 2.6 (potential irreducibility) and the non-solvable-image hypothesis on $\bar\rho$.

Both papers use Serre's invariants $k(\bar\rho)$ (Serre weight) and $N(\bar\rho)$ (prime-to-$p$ Artin conductor) defined in Serre 1987 (Duke). Paper A flags this as an external citation (DP392.8); paper B uses the same invariants tacitly throughout without giving them their own node. Aligning the cited external definition with paper B's implicit use; the underlying object is identical.

This is the centerpiece of the EXT relationship. Paper A's TP392.1 is the UNCONDITIONAL level-1 case of Serre's conjecture: every odd irreducible $\bar\rho$ unramified outside $p$ arises from $S_{k(\bar\rho)}(\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z}))$. Paper B's TP393.8 is the CONDITIONAL counterpart: modularity-lifting for level-1 crystalline lifts of weight $\in[2,2p]$ implies level-1 Serre. Same target conjecture, but paper A removes the lifting hypothesis. Marked analogous (not exact) because the assumptions differ (TP392.1 is unconditional, TP393.8 is conditional).

Paper A's CP392.1 is the (unconditional, after combining with TP392.1) modularity for prime-conductor weight-2 representations $\bar\rho$ of $G_\mathbb{Q}$. Paper B's TP393.9 is the conditional `killing-ramification' theorem reducing squarefree-conductor representations (with extra constraints) to level 1. Both occupy the same role: extending level-1 modularity to small-conductor cases. Paper B is conditional on the modularity-lifting hypothesis; paper A obtains the prime-conductor case unconditionally by combining TP392.1 with the relevant lifting results.

Paper A's finiteness corollary CP392.2 (only finitely many isomorphism classes of $\bar\rho$ unramified outside $p$) is a direct consequence of the unconditional level-1 Serre theorem and is not present in paper B (paper B has no analogous finiteness corollary; its analogous finiteness assertions concern abelian varieties via Schoof, which is a different statement).

Paper A's Proposition PrP392.1 (existence of weight-2 minimal lift for ordinary $\bar\rho$ with $2\le k(\bar\rho)\le p+1$, $k\neq p$) is essentially paper B's Theorem TP393.1 (existence of minimally ramified $p$-adic lift under the same hypotheses). Paper B's theorem is the broader / cleaner statement (covers crystalline and semistable types in weight $p+1$); paper A uses the special case in which the lift is forced to weight 2. Paper A explicitly cites paper B's machinery as [KW] for this result (proof PP392.1 invokes E3, E4 of Taylor [Tay3] together with Section 2.1 lifting machinery, which is paper B Section 2).

Paper A's Proposition PrP392.2 (Galois-theoretic analog of Carayol's lemma: lift with prescribed nebentype $\chi\eta_q^i$ at an auxiliary prime $q$) is a NEW construction in paper A, central to the second-lift step of the inductive procedure. Paper B does not contain such a `lift with chosen nebentype' result — it only constructs minimally ramified lifts. This is one of the main technical innovations distinguishing paper A from paper B.

Paper A's PrP392.3 (compatible system from a minimal lift, with parts (i) for the weight-2 minimal lift and (ii) for the Carayol-type lift with nebentype) is analogous to paper B's TP393.3 (Theorem `minimal': compatible system lifting a semistable $\bar\rho$, with parts (i) crystalline level-1 and (ii) semistable cases). Same role: produce a (weakly/strictly) compatible system from a constructed lift via Brauer + base change + Carayol-Taylor + Saito. Paper A's part (ii) (Carayol-with-nebentype) is paper-A specific; part (i) is essentially paper B's TP393.3(i).

Paper A's Lemma LP392.1 (Wintenberger's lemma on dihedral semistable mod-$p$ representations) is an arithmetic input specific to paper A's Chebyshev induction — it constrains which primes $p$ admit a level-1 dihedral semistable $\bar\rho$ of Serre weight $(p+1)/2$. Paper B does not extract this lemma. (Although attributed to Wintenberger, it is paper-A's lemma in this corpus.)
Paper A's `Weight reduction by twist' lemma is a local computation specific to the inductive weight-reduction procedure; no analog in paper B.

External citation (Breuil-Mezard / Savitt) used by paper A as a black box. Paper B does not re-cite this specific result. Per the prompt's compactness rule, external-origin nodes that are not aligned to other external nodes need not be matched, but this one is significant enough in paper A's argument that the absence in paper B is informative.

Paper A's Lemma LP392.4 (`Modularity for crystalline lifts when residual is modular' in level 1, weight even, $2\le k\le p+1$) is the inductive-step lifting result paper A applies when the residual is in the inductively-known weight range. It is a level-1 specialization of paper B's general modularity-lifting toolkit but is not itself a stated theorem in paper B (paper B uses Wiles / Taylor-Wiles / Skinner-Wiles / Kisin lifting theorems but does not assemble exactly this packaged lemma).
Paper A's `Propagation of modularity across primes for fixed weight' is a paper-A-specific organisational corollary used in the induction. No counterpart in paper B.
Chebyshev-prime existence remark, paper-A specific to the inductive procedure.

Key Chebyshev inequality (*) used in paper A's induction; paper B's induction (Theorem TP393.8) uses Bertrand's postulate $p_{n+1}\le 2p_n-1$ instead, which is a coarser inequality. Paper A's tighter quantitative estimate is an essential ingredient for the unconditional argument.

Local-form equations for $\bar\rho|_{I_p}$ in the ordinary case and for the weight-2 lift; these are computational descriptions inside paper A's lift construction. Paper B uses the same formalism implicitly but does not extract these specific equations.

Paper A's `Inductive weight-reduction strategy for level-1 Serre' is the central new algorithm of paper A: starting from $\bar\rho$ mod $p$, build a weight-2 minimal lift, place in compatible system, reduce mod a Chebyshev foil prime $\ell$, lift again with prescribed nebentype at $p$, reduce mod $p$, and use modularity lifting twice. Paper B has no analogous algorithm — its level-1 inductive proof (Theorem TP393.8) is conditional on a modularity-lifting hypothesis and uses Bertrand's postulate but no foil-prime / Chebyshev mechanism.

Both proofs (PP392.1 of PrP392.1 and PP393.1 of TP393.1) reduce the existence of the minimal lift to non-solvable image and then invoke the local versal-deformation-ring smoothness result (Ramakrishna / Taylor) plus Bockle's complete-intersection criterion. Same proof structure.

Proof of paper A's Carayol-analog proposition PrP392.2 uses an explicit Hensel-quadratic construction to verify $R_q$ smooth of relative dimension 1. No counterpart in paper B since PrP392.2 has no counterpart.

Both proofs construct a (strictly/weakly) compatible system from a minimal lift via Brauer + Arthur-Clozel base change (Taylor), then refine local properties using Carayol-Taylor, Breuil-Berger / Saito for the inertial WD parameters. Paper A's PP392.3 also adds (in part (ii)) a Raynaud + Saito + Breuil-Mezard / Savitt step for the auxiliary-prime nebentype case, which is paper-A specific.
Proofs of paper A's four `helper lemmas' (dihedral, Breuil-Mezard packaging, modularity for crystalline lifts in level 1) are paper-A specific; the underlying lemmas have no counterparts in paper B.
Proof of CP392.3 (propagation across primes); no counterpart.

These are the two papers' main level-1-Serre proofs and the heart of the EXT relationship. Paper B's PP393.13 (proof of TP393.8) is a CONDITIONAL induction on $p$ using Bertrand's postulate ($p_{n+1}\le 2p_n-1$) and the modularity-lifting hypothesis: given $\bar\rho$ mod $p_{n+1}$, build a strictly compatible system, look at the $p_n$-adic member of weight $\le 2p_n$, apply lifting hypothesis. Paper A's PP392.8 is the UNCONDITIONAL version: same outer induction skeleton, but each inductive step uses (i) a tighter Chebyshev inequality instead of Bertrand, (ii) two compatible systems linked at a foil prime $\ell$, (iii) explicit nebentype at $p$ via Carayol analog, (iv) Breuil-Mezard / Savitt to control the inductive residual weight. The strategies are conceptually analogous (both inductively reduce mod $p_{n+1}$ to mod $p_n$); paper A is the substantial unconditional refinement.

Composite L2 alignment between the inductive step DAGs of paper A (PP392.8) and paper B (PP393.13). Both inductive steps share three core moves: (a) lift $\bar\rho$ to a compatible system (PSP392.3 / PSP393.24), (b) reduce mod a smaller prime (PSP392.4 / PSP393.25 implicit), (c) apply modularity lifting (PSP392.10 / PSP393.25). Paper A's DAG is much longer because of the foil-prime construction (PSP392.4-7), the Carayol-analog second lift with chosen nebentype (PSP392.6), and the case analysis on the second residual representation (PSP392.5,8,9). Paper B's DAG simply applies Bertrand's postulate and the lifting hypothesis. Composite analogous match per the v2 prompt's allowed L2 pattern (parent first: PP392.8 ↔ PP393.13 above).

Proof of CP392.1 (modularity for prime conductor weight 2). Paper B has the conditional analog PP393.14 (proof of TP393.9), but the dependency / proof structure differs enough that we list these as none-paired here and rely on the CP392.1 ↔ TP393.9 match above for the L1 correspondence.
Proof of CP392.2 (finiteness): no counterpart in paper B.

Paper B's Theorem TP393.2 (universal deformation rings are finite flat complete intersections) is the central structural result of paper B's Section 2. Paper A uses this fact implicitly (it is cited via TP392.E2 as the Bockle appendix theorem) but does not state it as its own theorem; it appears in paper A only as the external Bockle citation.

Paper B's Proposition PrP393.1 (formal smoothness of $R_{p,\mathrm{crys}}$ in weight $p+1$ for tres ramifiee $\bar\rho$) is a key local-deformation input specific to paper B's foundational work on the existence of minimal lifts. Paper A relies on the conclusion (via citation of paper B / Taylor) but does not extract it as its own proposition.

Paper B's finiteness criterion via finite image (Lemma `finite') is a paper-B-specific deformation-theoretic lemma used inside the proof of TP393.2; paper A does not need this (it cites the global Bockle conclusion directly).

Paper B's Proposition `taylor' on potential automorphy is the explicit statement of the Taylor potential-automorphy input that paper A invokes via the external citation TP392.E1 (Taylor's potential modularity). Paper A does not give it a paper-origin node, so we list it as paper-B-only.
Paper B's potential-irreducibility lemma; supports PrP393.2. No counterpart in paper A.

Paper B's `low-level Serre' theorem (TP393.4: no Serre-type $\bar\rho$ in low conductors / weight $p+1$ for $p\in\{5,7,13\}$), classification of $(p,p)$-type group schemes (CP393.1), and `inexistence for small primes' (CP393.2: no $\bar\rho$ for $p\in\{2,3,5,7\}$) are unconditional results of paper B obtained via Schoof's theorem on semistable abelian varieties. Paper A's main theorem TP392.1 covers a broader set of cases unconditionally, but these specific small-prime / small-conductor inexistence results are paper-B contributions not separately stated in paper A.

Paper B's Theorem `lowweight' (no Serre-type $\bar\rho$ of level 1 with $k\in\{2,4,6,8,14\}$) is precisely the input that paper A cites as TP392.E9 (`KW low-weight cases of level-1 Serre'). The match is paper-A-external-citation (TP392.E9) ↔ paper-B-paper-result (TP393.5). Per the prompt's external-vs-paper guidance, this is a strong EXT signal but I emit it as a none entry on paper B's side because the natural pair is with the TP392.E9 citation node; see next entry.

Paper A's external citation TP392.E9 (`KW low-weight cases of level-1 Serre', stating Serre's level-1 conjecture in weights $\{2,4,6,8,12,14\}$) is exactly the union of paper B's main unconditional level-1 results: TP393.5 (no level-1 Serre type in $k\in\{2,4,6,8,14\}$), TP393.7 (weight-12 level-1 from Ramanujan $\Delta$), and TP393.4 (which contributes some of the small-prime inexistence). Paper A cites paper B as `[KW]' to use these as base cases of the induction. This is the textbook EXT signal: paper A's contribution is a level-1 theorem that absorbs paper B's level-1 theorem as the base of the induction.

Paper B's auxiliary `no irreducible crystalline $p$-adic representations in low weights' (TP393.6), `weight-11 from Ramanujan $\Delta$' (CP393.3), and `classification at $p\in\{11,13\}$' (CP393.4) are paper-B-specific corollaries / theorems flowing from TP393.4-5-7 and Schoof; not stated in paper A.
Already paired with paper A's CP392.1 above; this is a placeholder note acknowledging paper B's theorem. (Counted under the CP392.1 ↔ TP393.9 match.)

Paper B's two `modularity-lifting hypothesis' problems are precisely the conditional assumptions that paper A removes. Paper A doesn't carry them as `problem' nodes — it invokes the relevant lifting theorems (Wiles, Taylor-Wiles, Skinner-Wiles, Kisin) directly. The absence of counterparts in paper A is the EXT signal.

Paper A cites `Taylor's potential modularity' (TP392.E1) as an external theorem; paper B states the same theorem as Proposition PrP393.2 (the explicit Taylor-style potential-automorphy proposition). Paper A's external citation matches paper B's paper-origin proposition — a `paper-origin in B vs external in A' match, which (per the prompt's origin-aware guidance) is a strong EXT signal: paper B's own contribution is invoked by paper A as black-box prior work in the same way it cites Wiles or Taylor.
Both papers cite Bockle's complete-intersection criterion from his appendix to Khare [K03]. Identical external citation.
Both cite Wiles 1995 / Taylor-Wiles 1995 modularity lifting. Identical external citation.
Both cite Skinner-Wiles modularity lifting (residually reducible / nearly-ordinary). Identical external citation.
Paper A cites Kisin's modularity lifting (potentially Barsotti-Tate). Paper B does not list this as an external theorem, though Kisin's work is in the background. Listing as none on B-side.
Paper A cites Ribet-Edixhoven weight/level optimisation. Paper B does not break this out as an external theorem.

Paper A's external Tate level-1 mod-2 case is one of the four primes $p\in\{2,3,5,7\}$ covered by paper B's Corollary CP393.2 (no irreducible odd 2-dim mod-$p$ Galois reps unramified outside $p$). Paper B's CP393.2 absorbs and re-proves Tate's mod-2 result via its own machinery. Analogous match: same target conclusion, paper B re-derives it.
Paper A's external Serre mod-3 case is similarly covered by paper B's CP393.2 (which includes $p=3$). Analogous: same conclusion, different proof in paper B.

Paper B's external Taylor potential-automorphy theorem TP393.E2 is the same underlying result as paper A's TP392.E1 and paper B's own PrP393.2; already aligned via the TP392.E1 ↔ PrP393.2 match above.

Paper B cites Schoof's classification of semistable abelian varieties, central to its low-conductor results (TP393.4). Paper A does not invoke Schoof directly (paper A's Schoof connection is a remark RP392.3 about the historical motivation only).
Paper B cites Berger-Li-Zhu reductions; paper A also uses BLZ Corollary 4.1.3 inside proofs (e.g. PP392.6) but does not extract it as a separate external node.

Paper B cites Bertrand's postulate as the basis for its inductive bound. Paper A replaces this with the tighter Chebyshev inequality (paper-A nodes RP392.1, EP392.1) — a quantitative refinement essential for unconditioning the induction.
Paper B cites Fujiwara's $R=T$ over totally real fields. Paper A does not extract this as a separate external node, though Fujiwara's result is in the modularity-lifting toolkit invoked by paper A.
Paper B's standing-hypothesis assumption on Serre-weight range. Paper A makes the same assumption inside its propositions but does not extract it as a global node.
